verdict: Caution: lend selectively to GST-compliant, branded or value-added TMT re-rollers with verified turnover and monthly stock statements; avoid unbranded, thin-margin units with leveraged balance sheets and unresolved GST classification.
title: Mandi Gobindgarh steel re-rolling & TMT: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A re-roller buys sponge iron, scrap and billets, melts or reheats them, rolls TMT bars, and sells into construction demand within a few hundred kilometres.** Cash is made on the spread between input cost and re-bar price, not on volume alone; the Punjab GST take running +9.7% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D] tells you local sales are moving faster than the national average, so demand at the gate is real. **The catch is that this spread is thin and moves weekly with scrap and billet prices**, which is why rating reports flag sudden price fluctuations as a direct margin risk [8].

## Where value and cash actually sit
**Value sits in brand and in the conversion margin; cash sits in inventory and receivables.** A branded TMT player commands a premium over market rate through promotion and brand recall [7], while an unbranded re-roller sells at parity and lives on utilisation. Working capital is the real exposure: rating notes describe moderately high working capital requirements supported by bank lines [9], and gearing at one peer deteriorated to 1.80x from 1.40x on debt-funded acquisition and higher working capital borrowings [8]. **So when a proposal lands, check the inventory days and the creditor-to-debtor gap first; if the buyer list is dominated by government contractors with 90-day payment cycles, ask for the ageing and the bill-discounting history.**

## What has changed now
**The live issue is GST treatment of the secondary steel sector, not demand.** Local industry bodies have written to the Union Finance Minister seeking simplification after consulting Mandi Gobindgarh and Khanna units [1], which tells you classification and compliance friction is a current operating cost for these borrowers. Peer results are strong but come from other states: Steel Exchange India reported ~₹340 crore Q2 FY27 revenue, up ~45% YoY [4], and Rathi Steel crossed ₹200 crore with ~28.86% volume growth [5]; JSW Steel's consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue was ₹47,364 crore at 20% EBITDA margin [3]. **Treat these as proof the TMT cycle is healthy, not as evidence about Gobindgarh margins; the local GST note [1] is the only city-specific signal and it is about compliance, not pricing.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue re-rollers with GST-clean books, a branded or value-added product mix, and a captive or contracted billet source.** Avoid pure conversion job-workers with no brand and no raw-material linkage. Structure term debt against a defined capex with a moratorium matched to commissioning, and working capital against a drawing-power limit set from stock and debtor statements, not from projected turnover. **Take a monthly stock-and-debtor statement, a quarterly GST return reconciliation, and a monthly sales register by customer; if stock cover exceeds the sanctioned norm for two consecutive months, freeze the limit and inspect the yard.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for falling realisation per tonne alongside rising inventory, and for gearing creeping past the peer range.** A move from 1.40x to 1.80x happened at one peer in a single year [8]; if your borrower shows the same direction, ask for the debt-funded asset and its ramp-up plan. **If GST classification disputes or refund delays appear in the borrower's filings, treat it as a cash-flow event, not a tax event, and reprice or resize the limit.**
